column1: # Registry / handler parity rules — TAB separated, up to five columns:
#   name <TAB> source <TAB> extract-pattern (ERE) <TAB> target <TAB> transform (optional sed)
# Every token the pattern extracts from `source` must appear literally in
# `target`. The rule exists to make one failure impossible: something declared
# as supported before the code that implements it exists, so it parses fine,
# gets walked past at runtime, and is reported as having succeeded.
# `source` may carry a sed address range after the path to scope extraction to
# one block, e.g.  path/file.ts:/const SUPPORTED_TYPES/,/\]\);/
# Without a range the pattern matches the whole file, which usually produces
# false positives — a parser normally mentions type names outside its supported
# set, and none of those are meant to have handlers.
# `transform` is an optional sed expression applied to each extracted token,
# for when the registry and the implementation spell the same thing
# differently (e.g. "ext:HttpCall" in one file, "HttpCall" in the other).
# Paths are relative to the repository root. Rules whose source or target file
# does not exist are SKIPPED, so leaving examples in place is harmless.
# The other two gates (requirement coverage, constitution freshness) work in
# any Spec Kit project with no configuration. This third gate is inherently
# project-specific: only you know which registries must stay in step with an
# implementation. Uncomment and adapt.
# Put your project's rules in .specify/guard-parity-rules.tsv instead of editing
# this file — that path is outside the extension directory, so updating the
# extension cannot overwrite it.
# Example, from a workflow engine where a type registered in the parser but
# missing from the executor means a run silently skips a step and reports
# success:
# element types have executor handlers
# extension elements are declared in the schema
# Other shapes this fits:
#   - every route registered in a router has a handler module
#   - every event name emitted has a subscriber
#   - every feature flag referenced in code exists in the flag config
#   - every capability or tool listed in a registry has an implementation
